mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has climbed to a four-week high of +10.0 percent change while RETAIL_REC sits at -35.6, its weakest print in the window. A persistently elevated at-home share removes discretionary trip occasions, so the 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC will print below the prior 28-day mean of -31.8.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached +10.0 at t-0w, the highest of the four weekly means
regime_hint: stay-at-home regime with RESIDENTIAL sustained above +5
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the prior 28-day mean of -31.8 while RESIDENTIAL remains above +5 for every week of the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT fell 7.4 points week-on-week from -16.0 to -23.4, crossing below the -20 level that marked the milder weeks of the window. Commuter volumes below this threshold drain weekday footfall in transit-served retail districts, so the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean lands below the last.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 7 points week-on-week and crosses below -20
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -16.0 at t-1w to -23.4 at t-0w, a 7.4 point drop
failure_condition: TRANSIT stays below -20 for two consecutive weeks yet the subsequent 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is at or above the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-23.4) and WORKPLACES (-26.3) fall together in the same week, and the joint collapse of commuting removes both the transit-passing and office-lunch components of retail footfall. The interaction of the two series, not either alone, drives the decline in the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both below -20 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT (-23.4) and WORKPLACES (-26.3) sit below -20 at t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are jointly below -20, the following 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is above the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC alternates on a two-week cycle: mild weeks (t-3w -26.3, t-1w -30.1) and deep weeks (t-2w -35.3, t-0w -35.6). The latest print is a deep-week trough, so the following weeks revert toward the mild-week level and lift the 28-day mean above the prior one.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC prints below -33 in the most recent week
failure_condition: After a RETAIL_REC print below -33, the following week is also below that print, so no two-week-cycle rebound occurs.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM swings between positive and negative prints while RETAIL_REC stays deeply negative; positive grocery prints mark weeks when households consolidate outings into essential errands. That substitution persists, holding the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean below the last.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns positive while RETAIL_REC is below -20
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM printed +3.9 (t-3w) and +2.4 (t-1w), the two weeks with the milder RETAIL_REC prints
failure_condition: Weeks with GROCERY_PHARM positive and RETAIL_REC below -20 are followed by a higher 28-day RETAIL_REC mean than the preceding one.

failure_condition: A PARKS week-on-week gain of 5 points or more is not followed within one week by a RETAIL_REC print above -31.8.
